analysis: Documentation-only change in docs/architecture/inference.md. Changed lines in these units: head 542-544 (Nemotron Super image body cap described as 40 MiB with `media_too_large` instead of 8 MiB); other changed ranges (head 3, 128-132) are outside these units and describe the same cap raise for video. Surrounding text (head 416-1211) is unchanged context: Super memory/admission, prefix reuse partitioned by authenticated cache scope (head 530-532, consistent with T-041 / SEC-035 scoping), GLM5Next admission, calibration, CBv2 flow. The cap raise to 40 MiB is relevant to availability/memory (TB-007, T-029-type DoS), but docs state media reservation is taken from the shared budget before decoding and refused with 503 if not fitting (head 539-541), one image request at a time per owner with 429 (head 545-546), and that the 40 MiB body holds one 25 MiB inline-media part as base64. No source code is in this batch, so whether NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes actually changed to 40 MiB, and whether decode-memory bounds (pixel/decoded caps) remain enforced independent of encoded size, is unverified here; integration should check the Swift change (NemotronSuperServingPolicy, transports' 25 MiB inline-media cap) for consistent pre-decode limits. No threat-model regression identified from documentation alone; no confidentiality, attestation, or cache-scope semantics changed.
